title: Shah Rukh Khan Takes Full Ownership of His First Delhi Home
excerpt: The Bollywood superstar has acquired the remaining floors of his Panchsheel Park residence for ₹37 crore, completing ownership of the property where he and Gauri Khan began married life in 1991.
body:
• Shah Rukh Khan purchased the second and third floors of a residential building in South Delhi's Panchsheel Park for approximately ₹37 crore (around $4.4 million).
  • The Khan family already owned the basement and first floor, and the acquisition gives SRK sole ownership of the entire building.
  • The property was the couple's first marital home after their 1991 wedding, before Shah Rukh relocated to Mumbai to pursue acting.
  • Gauri Khan personally designed the home's interiors, including a "nostalgia wall" showcasing decades of family keepsakes.

Shah Rukh Khan has become the sole owner of the Delhi residence where he and wife Gauri Khan started their married life more than three decades ago. According to a report by Moneycontrol, the actor acquired the second and third floors of the residential building in South Delhi's upscale Panchsheel Park locality for an estimated ₹37 crore (roughly $4.4 million).

https://youtube.com/watch?v=ZUaeP63cXls

The Khan family already owned the basement and first floor of the property. With this latest transaction, the entire building — spread across a 1,200-square-yard plot (approximately 10,800 square feet) — is now under Shah Rukh's ownership. The underlying land has been valued at nearly ₹34,260 per square foot.

A Home Steeped in Personal History

The Panchsheel Park property holds deep sentimental value for the couple. It was the first home Shah Rukh and Gauri shared after their wedding on October 25, 1991. The couple solemnised their union through three ceremonies held on the same day — a registered civil marriage, a traditional Hindu wedding and a Nikah — before eventually relocating to Mumbai, where Shah Rukh pursued his film career full-time.

Over the years, Gauri has spoken openly about her emotional connection to the residence. In a widely cited interview with iDiva, she described the motivation behind designing the home.

"Our Delhi home is almost 20 years old. I am from Delhi and have lived a major part of my life here, so I thought it would be a great idea to buy and design a home close to my mom's house. The idea was to have all our memories under one roof."

— Gauri Khan, interior designer and producer

Gauri, who has built a parallel reputation as one of India's leading celebrity interior designers, personally designed the home's interiors. She has said that every corner of the house reminds her of different chapters of the family's life — from raising their three children, Aryan, Suhana and AbRam, to watching them grow into adults.

The Nostalgia Wall and a Family's Journey

One of the home's signature features is a dedicated "nostalgia wall" that showcases cherished keepsakes collected over the years, including childhood mementoes, Shah Rukh's artwork, postcards and thoughtful gifts exchanged within the family. Gauri has described it as a space where the family's treasured memories are preserved under one roof.

The acquisition is being regarded as one of the most notable celebrity residential property transactions in Delhi in recent years. It further consolidates the Khan family's growing portfolio of premium real estate, which spans properties in Mumbai — including the iconic Mannat bungalow in Bandra — as well as international destinations including Dubai.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For members of the Indian diaspora, the story resonates on a level beyond celebrity real estate. Many who left Indian cities for careers abroad understand the pull of a childhood or early-marriage home — the desire to hold on to a physical anchor of identity. Shah Rukh's decision to consolidate ownership of a property tied to the earliest years of his marriage, rather than simply acquiring new luxury assets, speaks to that emotional calculus.

Panchsheel Park remains one of South Delhi's most sought-after residential neighbourhoods, home to diplomats, senior bureaucrats and business families. Property prices in the area have surged over the past decade, making the ₹37-crore valuation notable but not unusual for a full-building acquisition in the locality.

What Comes Next

There has been no official statement from Shah Rukh Khan or his representatives about plans for the property. Whether the home will be renovated, preserved as-is or serve as a base for the family's Delhi visits remains to be seen. What is clear is that the Panchsheel Park residence — once the quiet starting point of one of Bollywood's most celebrated marriages — now belongs entirely to the man who left it decades ago to become India's biggest movie star.
